data.title: B1 Level Check
data.description: A mixed grammar check to estimate whether the learner is working securely at CEFR B1 level.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using the present perfect.
sections.explain: Use the present perfect for an unfinished time period or experience connected to the present. The correct form is 'have seen'.

words.word: I have seen that film three times.
I saw that film three times already.
I have saw that film three times.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct first conditional sentence.
sections.explain: In the first conditional, use the present simple after 'if' and 'will' in the main clause.

words.word: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
If it will rain tomorrow, we will stay at home.
If it rains tomorrow, we stay at home.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct second conditional sentence.
sections.explain: For an unreal or unlikely present situation, use 'if' + past simple and 'would' + base verb.

words.word: If I had more time, I would learn another language.
If I would have more time, I learned another language.
If I have more time, I would learn another language.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct reported speech sentence.
sections.explain: When reporting a past statement, the verb often moves back one tense. 'I am tired' becomes 'she was tired'.

words.word: She said that she was tired.
She said that she is tired yesterday.
She told that she was tired.

sections.explain: Use 'who' to introduce a relative clause describing a person.

words.word: The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
The woman which lives next door is a doctor.
The woman who she lives next door is a doctor.

sections.explain: The passive is formed with 'be' + past participle. The correct form is 'was built'.

words.word: The bridge was built more than fifty years ago.
The bridge built more than fifty years ago.
The bridge was build more than fifty years ago.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct modal verb for obligation.
sections.explain: 'Have to' is used for an obligation or requirement. After 'have to', use the base form of the verb.

words.word: I have to finish this report before Friday.
I have finish this report before Friday.
I have to finishing this report before Friday.

sections.explain: After a preposition such as 'in', use the -ing form. The correct structure is 'interested in learning'.

words.word: She is interested in learning more about photography.
She is interested in learn more about photography.
She is interested to learning more about photography.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct past continuous and past simple combination.
sections.explain: Use the past continuous for an action in progress and the past simple for the shorter action that interrupted it.

words.word: I was driving home when I saw the accident.
I drove home when I was seeing the accident.
I was driving home when I was seeing the accident.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct present perfect sentence using 'for'.
sections.explain: For a situation that started in the past and continues now, use the present perfect with 'for' plus a period of time.

words.word: They have lived in this town for eight years.
They live in this town since eight years.
They lived in this town for eight years and still live here.
